verdict.rationale: Epic's docs cover packaging one project for every supported platform: one-click deploy to iOS and Android, Unreal Frontend for deploying to consoles, and a cook command that targets several platforms at once (-targetplatform=<Plat1>+<Plat2>). The license page lists "All platforms & features." Coverage is incomplete because desktop targets are never named as export destinations and nothing documents how console access works. missing for 10: explicit documentation of desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux) packaging targets, documented console access or partner/SDK terms, independent hands-on corroboration of shipping one project to desktop, mobile and console.

support.subject: As a studio lead, one project exports to desktop, mobile, and (directly or via partners) consoles

citations.quote: This section contains guides for packaging and releasing projects for all of the platforms that Unreal Engine supports.
Launching to Devices — One-click deploying your project to devices like iOS and Android for testing
Unreal Frontend — Tool for managing applications and deploying to consoles.
This command can cook content for a platform, package it up into a platform's native format for distribution, deploys it to the device, and automatically runs the project
